newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS Europe region to be managed from London.
newsitem.headline: UBS Europe region to be managed from London.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland said that it was moving two senior executives to new posts, which will also mean that its European regional operations will be managed from London in future.
"Basically, London is the predominant financial centre. We are not going to try and fight against market forces," said UBS chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta.
"From now on, UBS Region Europe will be managed out of London," Cabiallavetta said.
Cabiallavetta said that David Robins will head UBS's European regional operations in future.
Robins will take the place of Felix Zumbach, the current head of Europe who was based in Zurich.
Zumbach will now head UBS's "largest and economically strongest region -- Zurich," Cabiallavetta said.

Robins, a British citizen, was named as chief executive of UBS UK Ltd in January 1994. Prior to that, he held other posts within the bank in Zurich and New York, and also worked at UBS Phillips & Drew International in Tokyo as head of research from 1986 to 1988.
UBS purchased the majority of Phillips and Drew in 1986.

Cabiallavetta said London's position as the predominant European financial centre was reinforced by its place between Asia and North America in world time zones, and due to its high level of market liquidity.

Werner Bonadurer, UBS chief of securities trading, said that defacto London had already served as the headquarters for UBS's European investment operations, adding some senior executives had already gradually been shifted to London from Zurich.
He said it came down to the issue of "decentralising" within the bank. "The market forces are clearly bringing this business more and more to London," he said.
